correctness.rationale: In the union of allowed arrows, a k-step walk would give a nonzero k-fold product. Longest-path levels therefore embed S in a complete ordered layered semigroup, splitting levels if needed when n>=k. Each labeled chain is uniquely ordered by its occupied levels, giving the exponential formula including singleton chains. Extracting the two layer variables from exp(F0+(x+y)F1+xyF2) gives the nonnegative terms (a)_d(b)_d F1^(a+b-2d) F2^d/d!, with exp(F0) common. Each existing factor pair increases by a-b-1 under the transfer and any additional term is nonnegative. The single-arrow count increases strictly, and a proper subsemigroup has smaller cardinality; symmetry gives the converse equality. The rank-of-powers formula and second-difference inverse follow chain by chain. The recorded small checks are illustrative, not used as an all-size proof.
residual_risks: Scoped to partial injections, labeled maps and a uniform bound on products of elements; no claim about the full partial transformation monoid.

originality.rationale: The narrower rank-polynomial statement alone cannot recover the chain-profile inequalities, but its published proof is already profile-preserving. The predecessor's marked-vertex recoloring leaves the partition itself unchanged and explicitly preserves every block size. Restrict its double count to any fixed full block-size multiset and the same ratio, monotone at every shared-block stratum h, proves the claimed coefficientwise transfer. The prior chain/partition bijection and exponential construction also give the new EGF by giving a block of size j weight u_j rather than t^(j-1). Its single-arrow strictness and cardinality equality criterion give the full equality case. The frozen formal-series argument is another derivation, not a new extremal conclusion.
residual_risks: No claim of historical priority for the predecessor's proof; other sources could also contain the result. No indexed exact-profile title is needed for the demonstrated implication.
